newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 22.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Super League plans to include a team in Melbourne next year. The announcement comes after months of heavy negotiations. The Australian Rugby League is also considering putting a team in Melbourne, but recently delayed the decision until at least next month. Page 22.

Collingwood's plan to play their away matches at the Homebush Stadium in Sydney after the 2000 Olympics was criticised by rival Australian Football League clubs yesterday, as it would probably involve other teams giving up their home games. Collingwood are interested in tapping into the supporter base in Sydney. Page 22.

Young Australian basketballers Chris Anstey and Sam Mackinnon have been described by leading American coach Lute Olson as certainties for the National Basketball Association in the United States. He made the comment after the Australian Under-23s were beaten by the University of Arizona 79-76. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Rugby Union agreed yesterday to grant the Australian Capital Territory Brumbies financial parity with Queensland and New South Wales. The ACT officials have lobbied the ARU for the deal due to concern they would lose key players at the end of this Super 12 season, and as they struggle to remain competitive. Page 46.

Australian Olympic Committee president John Coates has called on the International Amateur Athletics Federation to review the penalties for drug use in sport, after sprinter Dean Capobianco was banned for four years after testing positive to steroids. Athetes from some European countries could only be banned for two years, due to their governments' right-to-work laws. Page 43.

The New South Wales Rugby Union has given Eastern Suburbs' Waratah five-eighth Scott Bowen conditional clearance to play in their match against Manly on Saturday, even though he only has 40 per cent use of an arm which was badly injured last year. Bowen'sprogress will be monitored each day, with a final decision made after an examination tomorrow. Page 45.
THE AGE

Essendon Australian Football League player Michael Long underwent a second reconstruction on his right knee last night, after an injury sustained in last weekend's game against St Kilda. It was the third major operation on the knee in four years. Long was determined to continue playing, though he acknowledged his style of play and role in the team would have to change. Page B8.

The Australian men's basketball team, the Boomers, won last night's game against Croatia 96-79 after trailing 43-41 at half-time. Australia's victory sealed the five-game series, following wins in Newcastle and Melbourne in the opening two rounds. Page B6

The Australian Football League was considering testing a proposed rule change to stop the growing trend for scrums of players to fall on the ball, resulting in more ball-ups. The rule would penalise players who do not knock the ball on once they have fallen to their knees. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Two umpires have been dropped by the Australian Football League after some controversial decisions in last Sunday's Brisbane-Fremantle game at Subiaco Oval. Michael Avon and Mark Prince were demoted for last week's game and other recent performances. Brisane lost the game by five points when Fremantle kicked a goal after the final siren. Page 84.

Sydney United may be expelled in an effort to eradicate hooliganism from Australian soccer. Soccer Australia chairman David Hill said Sydney United and South Melbourne would be charged with bringing the game into disrepute after crowd disturbances at thei match last Sunday. Most of the video evidence shows incidents involving Sydney fans. Sydney United plays in the Ericsson Cup grand final on Sunday. Page 81.

An international sporting program for Sydney, covering all 28 Olympic sports, was announced yesterday for the year leading up to the 2000 Olympics. The programme will be used as a dress rehearsal and those sports where Australia is less successful will be given particularly close examination. Page 79.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Illawarra forward Craig Smith, making his State of Origin debut with the Queensland team next week, has not been able to run with his team. Smith is suffering from severe bruising to the thigh, but is expected to start running with the team on Saturday or Sunday, and will have a full training session leading into the game. Page 92.

Channel Seven has decided not to broadcast the Sydney Swans Australian Football League games live until the Swans matches were on at more consistent times, allowing regular programming. Seven is playing delayed broadcasts. Seven sports directorAlan Batema said that as the season progressed and the Swans had more home games, the move would be made to live broadcasts. Page 94.

Australia's world champion women's water polo team has failed in its campaign to have their sport included in the Sydney 2000 Olympics. A decision by the International Olympic Committee to include new events in synchronised swimming and shooting means women's water polo will not be admitted. Page 95.
